items.kind: language design (M–L): impl heads over every array length
items.title: A161's premise does not hold: std cannot write `[T; n]`'s `Items<T>` impl — an impl subject's array LENGTH is an integer literal (`parse_array_length`), so there is no head that covers every length; the door is a length-erased head (`impl [type T; _] with Items<T>`) or I2's const-generic lengths
items.body: `xs.push_many(a)` over `a: [i32; 3]` is refused "'[i32; 3]' does not implement trait 'Items<i32>'", and no std impl can fix it: `Type::Array(element, usize)` carries a literal length, every comparator (`compare_type`, `compare_type_rigid`, impl_select's `elements_agree`) compares lengths by value, and the native backend monomorphizes on types (`write_type_key` writes `Arr[T;3]`, `rust_type` writes `[T; 3]`), so an any-length head would need (1) a length binder or wildcard in impl-subject position, (2) the comparators to admit it, (3) mono to key the instance by the receiver's concrete length and substitute it into `self`'s type, and (4) a rule for what `self.len()` means inside (today `.len()` folds to the literal, fixed-arrays.md §10). That is the narrow half of I2 (blocked on what `const N` means); the narrow door asks only 'every length', never names `N`. Natively F109 (an annotated array literal emits `vec![..]`) blocks any differential first. Also met: B582 (an array impl head's element binder). Rec: rule whether the length-erased head is worth its own slice ahead of I2; until then A161 stays open and `push_many(a.iter())` is not available either (arrays have no `iter()`). Sizing M–L; parser + solver + mono + both emitters.

items.title: an impl head over a fixed array cannot bind its element: `impl [type T; 3] with Count { .. }` is refused "cannot find type 'T'" at both `T`s, while `impl [i32; 3] with Count` compiles (B177) and impl selection already binds through an array's element (`bind_subject`'s and `collect_subject_binders`' `Type::Array` arms)
items.body: The subject-binder registration walk that admits `type T` in an impl head (struct arguments, tuples) does not descend into `Node::ArrayType`, so the binder is never declared and every mention of it is unresolved. Selection is ready for it: `impl_select::bind_subject` binds `T = i32` from `[T; n]` against `[i32; n]`. Fix: the registration walk's array arm. Repro: finds/array_impl_element_binder.vl (`vilan run` refuses; with `[i32; 3]` it runs on JS — natively F109 refuses the caller's literal). Sizing S; solver.

items.title: a fragment written directly inside a fragment is refused with the list literal's bare element mismatch — "Expected View (this literal's element type), but got List<View> instead." — with no word that it is a fragment or that nesting goes through a child position (Building UI, Fragments, says so)
items.body: E272 (std-48) steers a fragment that lands where ONE `View` is wanted at a return, a `let`, an argument and a field (`with_fragment_steer`). The list literal's own element check is a fifth site with its own sentence, and a nested fragment reaches it: `<>"a"<>"b"`. Rec: the same marker (a list literal whose span opens with `<`) at the element check, with "a fragment does not flatten into a fragment: put the inner one in a child position (`…`), or spread its children into the outer one". Repro: finds/fragment_in_fragment.vl. Sizing XS; the list literal's element check.

items.title: the type of `null` cannot be written: `let nothing: null = null;` is refused "found 'null' expected a type in type annotation", while diagnostics print the type by that name ("Expected i32, but got null instead.") and `std::js::null` declares it (`external struct null;`)
items.body: `null` is a keyword token, and the type grammar takes names; the global scope binds the primitive `null` (analyzer's primitive-struct table, `("null", "js::null")`) but no source spelling reaches it. Met while closing B555 (the module cannot be imported for the same reason). Question for the owner: is `null`'s type meant to be unwritable (a value only, with `void` the unit type), or should the type grammar take the keyword? If unwritable, the mismatch could say so rather than name a type the author cannot write. Repro: finds/null_in_type_position.vl. Sizing S.

items.title:
an `Option` is not a `Slot`, so `

"item"{badge}

` over `badge: Option` is refused (E271's "a hole in element syntax takes a `View`, a `str`, a `List` or a `Source` of one, and `badge` is `Option`"); `Some(view)` placing the view and `None` placing nothing would be the static twin of `when`
items.body: The child contract (B268) is `View`, `str`, `List<View>` and a `Source` of each. An optional child is written today as a `match` in the hole, `.show(..)`, or `when(..)` for the reactive case. Whether `impl Option<type V: Slot> with Slot` (both twins) belongs in the contract is the owner's: it is one arm, and `Source<Option<View>>` would follow from the blanket. Repro: finds/option_view_hole.vl. Sizing S; std (both ui twins).
